text:
emily: Heads-up — post-canary we’re seeing a persistent drop in signal-to-noise on the 'long-seq' slice. Not huge but visible across several metrics. anyone else seeing this?
jamal: on it. which metric specifically? p50/p95/p99s or quality signals?
emily: p99 latency +30ms, 95->99 gap widened, and a small increase in hallucination-rate (0.15%). baseline traffic looks stable.
sasha: can you paste the dashboard link and the traffic split?
emily: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/84?slice=long-seq — traffic-split to v2 = 12% for canary. deploy-bot: "deploy: rollout v2 started (canary=12%) by @emily at 1999994321"
jamal: interesting. the guard should have tripped at 0.5% degrad, why didn't it?
emily: guard was configured against absolute error counts incorrectly — we recently changed ingestion key names and the guard rule matched the old metric. so alerts were silent. :facepalm:
priya: that explains silence. we should make guards resilient to metric renames — maybe match by semantic tags instead of string keys.
sasha: agree. also the SNR drop looks concentrated on requests with sequence_length > 1024. Could be kernel selection/compilation path for long context.
jamal: can we confirm routing? are long-seq requests being routed to a different backend pool (eg. node-type A) under the new policy?
emily: yes, routing policy v2 introduced a small affinity rule to prefer pool-a for v2 models to reduce cold-starts. pool-a has a different batcher config.
rick: different batcher config + long seq = bigger KV cache churn -> higher p99. we saw similar with quantized models last year.
priya: proposal: expand canary telemetry to include slice-aware SNR and batching metrics (batch-size distribution, kv-cache hit rate). That would surface this faster.
sasha: +1. need a quick query to validate hypothesis. jamal, can you run a timeseries grouping by seq_len_bucket + backend_pool?
jamal: running now, snippet: ```select time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, seq_len_bucket, backend_pool, avg(latency_p99) from inference_metrics where rollout='v2' group by 1,2,3 order by 1 desc limit 50;```
emily: results look like backend_pool=pool-a has p99 +40ms for seq_len>1024, pool-b stable.
priya: ok action items: (1) pause canary traffic-split to 5% and rollback pool affinity for v2; (2) fix guard rule to use rate-based metric; (3) add new slice telemetry (batching + kv hits) to the canary dashboard; (4) run an A/B small experiment to validate batcher tweak.
rick: I can push a quick guard patch and add the slice charts to the canary dashboard. will coordinate with observability.
sasha: UX note — in console rollout UI we should show an explicit 'slice SNR' quick-check before approving traffic increases. Maybe a compact card that shows delta vs baseline and whether guard would have fired.
emily: love that. helps non-SRE reviewers decide.
jamal: one more thing — add a lightweight smoke eval that runs on the canary slice (long-seq) that checks hallucination/regression; run it every 5m.
priya: I'll file a brief RFC to make guard rules resilient and to standardize slice identifiers across telemetry.
deploy-bot: "alert: guard-rule-update applied by rick at 1999994470"
emily: thanks team. I'll reduce split to 5% now and watch for regression. updates in 10m.
sasha: ping when you reduce split, i'll watch dashboards.
emily: split reduced to 5% — https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/328 — watching :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jamal: metrics trending back toward baseline already on pool-b traffic. pool-a still elevated.
priya: leaving this thread with the action list. we'll sync in the rollout retrospective tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
